verdict.rationale: The SDK's Structured Outputs feature lets developers define a schema and the SDK validates the agent's JSON output against it, re-prompting on mismatch — a form of schema validation catching mistakes, but this happens at runtime/re-prompt time, not at compile/build time. There is no evidence of static/compile-time type checking (e.g., TypeScript strict-mode enforcement of tool schemas) that would catch an agent's own mistakes before execution. Missing for 10: build-time/compile-time type validation, TypeScript strict typing enforcement over tool calls, independent confirmation that schema mismatches are caught pre-runtime rather than via re-prompt.
